explain.say: The Ramayana is one of the two great epics of India. It tells the journey of Prince Rama of Ayodhya, his wife Sita and his brother Lakshmana, and it is traditionally said to be the work of the poet sage Valmiki.

draw.text: About 24,000 verses in 7 books, in Sanskrit
Tradition calls Valmiki the first poet, the Adi Kavi

explain.say: King Dasharatha had promised his queen Kaikeyi two wishes, and she asked that Rama be sent to the forest for 14 years. Rama accepted to keep his father's word, and Sita and Lakshmana went with him.

draw.text: Bharata ruled in Rama's name, placing Rama's sandals on the throne

explain.say: In the forest, Ravana, the ten headed king of Lanka, carried Sita away. Rama and Lakshmana searched for her and made friends with Sugriva and the monkey hero Hanuman, who leapt across the sea to find her.

draw.label: Rama's journey from Ayodhya south to Lanka, traditionally identified with Sri Lanka (route simplified)

explain.say: Rama's army built a bridge to Lanka, and after a great battle Ravana was defeated and Sita was freed. Rama returned home to Ayodhya and was crowned king, a return that many Hindus celebrate with lamps at Diwali.

draw.text: Dussehra marks Rama's victory; Diwali, in many places, his return

explain.say: Valmiki's poem has seven books, called kandas, from Rama's childhood to his later life as king. For many Hindus, Rama shows the ideal of dharma: a son, husband, brother and ruler who does what is right.

items: Aranya | Forest life, Sita is taken
Kishkindha | Friendship with Sugriva and Hanuman
Sundara | Hanuman finds Sita in Lanka

explain.say: Many scholars date Valmiki's poem to around the 5th to 1st century BCE, with later additions. The story has been retold again and again, by Tulsidas in Hindi, Kamban in Tamil, and in Thailand, Cambodia and Indonesia.

items: Many scholars: Valmiki's epic, about 5th to 1st century BCE

draw.text: Dates are scholars' estimates; tradition places Rama far earlier

faq.a: The Ramayana is traditionally said to be the work of the sage Valmiki, who is honoured as the first poet of Sanskrit. Scholars think his poem grew over several centuries, with some parts added later.
asks: Who is the author of the Ramayana?

faq.q: What is the story of the Ramayana?
faq.a: Prince Rama is sent into the forest for 14 years with his wife Sita and brother Lakshmana. The demon king Ravana carries Sita off to Lanka, and Rama, helped by Hanuman and an army of monkeys and bears, rescues her and returns to rule Ayodhya.
asks: Tell me the story of Rama and Sita

faq.a: Valmiki's Ramayana has about 24,000 verses, arranged in seven books called kandas. It is about a quarter of the length of the Mahabharata.
asks: How many verses are in the Ramayana?
How many kandas does the Ramayana have?
How many books are in the Ramayana?

faq.q: Why was Rama sent into exile?
faq.a: King Dasharatha had once promised Queen Kaikeyi two wishes. She asked that her son Bharata be king and that Rama go to the forest for 14 years, and Rama went willingly so his father would keep his word.
asks: Why did Rama go to the forest?
Why was Rama exiled for 14 years?

faq.a: Hanuman is a hero of the monkey people, famous for his strength, courage and devotion to Rama. He leaps across the sea to Lanka to find Sita, and many Hindus worship him as a model of loyal devotion.
asks: Who was Hanuman in the Ramayana?

faq.a: Ravana is the powerful king of Lanka in the Ramayana, often shown with ten heads. Many retellings also show him as a great scholar and devotee of Shiva, but his pride and his capture of Sita lead to his fall.
asks: Why does Ravana have ten heads?

faq.a: Sita is Rama's wife, the daughter of King Janaka of Mithila, found as a baby in a furrow of the earth. She is honoured for her courage and faithfulness, and many Hindus revere her as a goddess.
asks: Who was Sita in the Ramayana?

faq.q: Where is Lanka in the Ramayana?
faq.a: In the story Lanka is Ravana's island kingdom across the sea, south of India. It is traditionally identified with the island of Sri Lanka, though scholars debate whether Valmiki meant the same place.
asks: Is Lanka the same as Sri Lanka?

faq.q: What are the seven kandas of the Ramayana?
faq.a: They are the Bala, Ayodhya, Aranya, Kishkindha, Sundara, Yuddha and Uttara kandas. They follow Rama from childhood, through exile, the search for Sita and the war, to his reign as king.
asks: What are the books of the Ramayana?
Name the kandas of the Ramayana

faq.a: The Ramcharitmanas is a retelling of Rama's story written by the poet Tulsidas in the 1500s, in Awadhi, a form of Hindi. It is loved and recited across north India and is the basis of many Ramlila plays.
asks: Is the Ramcharitmanas the same as the Ramayana?

faq.q: How is the Ramayana connected to Diwali?
faq.a: In many parts of India, Diwali celebrates Rama, Sita and Lakshmana returning to Ayodhya, when the people lit rows of lamps to welcome them. Dussehra, a few weeks earlier, marks Rama's victory over Ravana.
asks: Why do people light lamps for Rama?

faq.q: Is the Ramayana told in other countries?
faq.a: Yes. The story spread across Asia and is retold as the Ramakien in Thailand, the Reamker in Cambodia, the Hikayat Seri Rama in Malaysia and the Kakawin Ramayana in Java, often in dance and shadow puppet theatre.
asks: Is the Ramayana famous outside India?

faq.a: For many readers the Ramayana teaches dharma, doing what is right even when it is hard. Rama is seen as an ideal son and king, Sita as faithful and brave, Lakshmana and Hanuman as loyal, and Ravana's fall as a warning about pride.
asks: What is the moral of the Ramayana?
What lessons does the Ramayana teach?

faq.a: Many scholars date Valmiki's Ramayana to roughly the 5th to 1st century BCE, with the first and last books probably added later. Hindu tradition places the life of Rama much earlier, in a past age called the Treta Yuga.
asks: Is the Ramayana older than the Mahabharata?

facts: Valmiki's Ramayana has about 24,000 verses in seven books called kandas.
Tradition honours Valmiki as the Adi Kavi, the first poet of Sanskrit.
Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas, a retelling of the Ramayana in Awadhi, in the 1500s.
Rama's exile in the forest lasts 14 years.
The Ramayana is retold in Southeast Asia as the Ramakien in Thailand and the Reamker in Cambodia.

quiz.say: Who is traditionally said to have composed the Ramayana?
quiz.show: Who is the traditional author of the Ramayana?
quiz.why: The Ramayana is traditionally the work of the sage Valmiki, honoured as the first poet.

wrong.0: Vyasa is the traditional author of the Mahabharata, the other great epic.
wrong.2: Kalidasa was a later classical poet and playwright, not the author of the Ramayana.
wrong.3: Hanuman is a hero inside the story, not its author.

quiz.say: Rama agrees to go into exile so that his father can keep a promise. Which value is the story showing here?
quiz.show: Rama accepts exile so his father keeps his word. What value does this show?

options.say: Keeping your word and doing your duty

quiz.why: Rama puts duty and his father's promise above his own claim to the throne, which is why many see him as an ideal of dharma.

wrong.1: Rama gives up power here; he leaves the throne behind.
wrong.2: There is no revenge in this choice; Rama does not blame Kaikeyi or Bharata.

quiz.say: The Ramayana is told as the Ramakien in Thailand and as shadow puppet plays in Indonesia. What does this suggest about the story?
quiz.show: Why might the Ramayana be retold in so many cultures?

options.show: Its themes of duty and loyalty travel well
options.say: Its themes of duty, loyalty and good against evil speak to many people

quiz.why: Traders, teachers and artists carried the story across Asia, and each culture made it its own because its themes speak to people everywhere.

wrong.1: It was never banned; it has always been loved in India.
wrong.2: It is an ancient epic, more than two thousand years old.
